claim_being_audited: That certifying the model now is compliant and evidentially supported despite the aviation maintenance triage evaluation gap, based mainly on aggregate readiness results, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance guidance on documenting and monitoring risks.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the policy threshold, including any required disclosure or approved risk acceptance for a material weakness.
Treat the aviation maintenance triage gap as material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; low-volume or non-core labels do not defeat that predicate.
Generic evidence of aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents can support operational readiness, but not override a specific unresolved disclosure obligation.
An open legal review on a named use-case limitation weighs against concluding the action is fully supported.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the aviation maintenance triage gap must be disclosed before launch.
The actual model card or release disclosure showing the named limitation was disclosed, if disclosure has already occurred.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case, if the team intends to launch before the gap is resolved.
Underlying customer commitment records tying the aviation maintenance triage segment to the two airline deployments, to confirm contractual materiality scope.
specific_concerns: The affected aviation maintenance triage segment misses target by 1.1 percentage points and is named in two airline deployment commitments, which makes the weakness plausibly material under the stated policy.
The policy text states that product labels like non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no admissible evidence shows either disclosure completion or approved risk acceptance.
Public governance guidance about documentation and monitoring is generic and does not substitute for satisfaction of the internal disclosure policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on current evidence without first resolving whether the named-segment gap requires disclosure.
That the named-segment issue is immaterial or can be overcome by aggregate readiness evidence alone.
That public model-card and risk-management guidance independently support waiving or deferring the policy requirement tied to a named launch use case.
